title: Emiliano Montalvo Vásquez
text:
Hi! I am an Economist and Researcher with experience across applied research, data science consulting, public policy, and data-driven social projects. I hold a double degree in Economics and Government and Public Transformation from Tecnológico de Monterrey.
My work combines quantitative methods, econometrics, data science, and geospatial analysis to study economic and public policy challenges. I have applied R and Python to statistical analysis, econometric modeling, machine learning, text mining, web scraping, geospatial analysis, and R Shiny development.
My research interests include political economy, public opinion, subnational democracy, public policy, and applied econometrics.

title: Research Experience
text:
Subnational Politics Project — Tecnológico de Monterrey
Student Researcher
Mar. 2026 – Aug. 2026
Supervisors: Dr. Agustina Giraudy; Dr. Francisco Urdinez; MPP(c) Felipe I. Soto Jorquera
Built PROSPER, a historical subnational dataset covering GDP, population, and GDP per capita for 83 second-tier administrative units across Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico from 1980 to 2024. Developed data harmonization, interpolation, and spatial processing procedures to construct comparable longitudinal indicators across countries and administrative boundaries. Documented data construction procedures and research design in a forthcoming codebook and working paper.
Methods: Data Harmonization · Interpolation · Economic Reconstruction · Spatial Data Processing · Longitudinal Data Construction
Tools: R · Data Engineering · Geospatial Analysis

Department of Economics — Tecnológico de Monterrey
Student Researcher & Project Manager
Jul. 2025 – Present
Supervisors: Dr. David Valenzuela Vega; Dr. Carlos Saldaña Villanueva
Conduct research on U.S.–China trade flows using econometric and machine learning methods for forecasting and empirical analysis. Led a multidisciplinary student research team and developed reproducible statistical programming workflows in R and Python. The project has contributed to a manuscript accepted for publication and to presentations at international and national academic conferences.
Methods: Econometric Modeling · Machine Learning · Time-Series Forecasting
Tools: R · Python · LSTM · Econometrics · Data Visualization


Department of Political Science — Tecnológico de Monterrey
Student Researcher
Sep. 2024 – Jul. 2025
Supervisors: Dr. Juan Carlos Montero Bagatella; Dr. Carlos Saldaña Villanueva
Conducted empirical research on the relationship between presidential political communication and public opinion in Mexico. Applied natural language processing and text analysis to presidential communications and combined these data with time-series regression models to examine changes in presidential approval. The research contributed to a peer-reviewed article examining the relationship between presidential rhetoric and public opinion.
Methods: Natural Language Processing · Text Analysis · Time-Series Regression · Political Communication Analysis
Tools: R · Text Mining · Econometrics

Research Assistant

Conducted quantitative analysis of trade, investment, and employment data for an applied research project examining the economic implications of nearshoring. Developed reproducible data-processing and analytical workflows in R and Quarto and contributed to the preparation of research outputs.
Methods: Quantitative Analysis · Data Cleaning · Descriptive Statistics
Tools: R · Quarto · Data Analysis

Project Manager & Research Assistant

title: Research Outputs
text:
Álvarez-Salas, M., Huitz-Montero, O. A., Montalvo-Vásquez, E., Valenzuela Vega, D. R., & Saldaña Villanueva, C. E.
Trendinomics, 2(2), 1–12.
🔗 Article


Abstract

This study develops a forecasting framework to improve the prediction of international trade flows under increasing geopolitical uncertainty, trade tensions, and global value chain fragmentation.




Rodríguez Bedolla, J., Samano Rodríguez, J. M. A., Huerta Treviño, A. I., & Montalvo Vásquez, E.
Revista Estudiantil de Economía.
Accepted


Abstract

This study examines the effect of childcare use on household socioeconomic well-being in southern Mexico using ENUT 2024, an AMAI-based socioeconomic index, and an IPWRA model to estimate treatment effects while accounting for selection bias and territorial differences.




Montalvo Vásquez, E., Saldaña, C., & Montero Bagatella, J. C.
Revista Mexicana de Opinión Pública, 20(39), 43.
🔗 Article


Abstract

This study examines the relationship between presidential rhetoric and approval ratings in Mexico, finding a statistically significant negative association between the rhetoric of the daily presidential conferences and presidential approval.

title: Research Outputs
text:
Working Papers & Research Projects

PROSPER Dataset Codebook: Historical Reconstruction of Subnational GDP, Population, and GDP Per Capita Data — Subnational Politics Project (SPP)
Giraudy, A., Montalvo Vásquez, E., Barrientos Villa, P. Y., & Soto Jorquera, F.
Subnational Politics Project (SPP).
Working Paper · Forthcoming
↗ PROSPER Dashboard


Abstract

This project develops PROSPER, a harmonized long-run panel of GDP, population, and GDP per capita for 83 second-tier subnational units across Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico. The project extends the Subnational Politics Project’s data infrastructure through the standardized reconstruction and harmonization of heterogeneous historical economic series.



The Relation Between Political-Criminal Violence and Subnational Democratic Backsliding in Mexico — 2026
Montalvo Vásquez, E.
Undergraduate Thesis, Tecnológico de Monterrey.
↗ ResearchGate


Abstract

This study examines the relationship between political-criminal violence and subnational democratic backsliding across Mexican states.



El Rincón de Siempre: una propuesta de cuidado comunitario y participación social en la vejez — 2026
Montalvo Vásquez, E. & Delgado Pérez, D.
Conversatorio Internacional Ciudad, Cuidados y Vejez 2026, Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México.
🔗 Paper


Abstract

This policy proposal presents a community initiative to reduce urban elderly social isolation in San Pedro.



Exploring the Role of Coping Mechanisms and Professional Experience in Job Placement Perception Among University Students: A Case Study from Tecnológico de Monterrey — 2025
Montalvo-Vásquez, E., García-Rojas, A., & Martínez-Canseco, J. S.
Monterrey International Book Fair 2025 (FILMTY 2025).
🔗 Paper


Abstract

This study investigates student perceptions at Tecnológico de Monterrey, finding that students prioritize academic knowledge over coping mechanisms when evaluating job placement prospects.

title: Recommendations
text:
Full-time Faculty, Universidad de Monterrey (UDEM)

“I first met Emiliano Montalvo as a student in the early semesters of his Government and Public Transformation program at Tecnológico de Monterrey. Years later, at Universidad de Monterrey, I had the opportunity to collaborate with him as a co-author of an academic article. Witnessing his transition from student to research colleague has been deeply rewarding.
Emiliano has always stood out for his intelligence, intellectual curiosity, and discipline. His academic training enables him to analyze complex problems from different perspectives while maintaining rigorous methodological standards.
As a researcher, he stands out for his analytical ability, academic rigor, and willingness to learn. During our collaboration, he demonstrated a strong ability to conduct empirical research, work with advanced quantitative tools, and translate complex questions into evidence.
Beyond his academic talent, Emiliano is responsible, proactive, and highly committed to the quality of his work. I am confident that he will continue to stand out for his talent, capacity to learn, and commitment to generating useful and relevant knowledge.”
